mobbin:8914ef26-a0a5-4618-a806-8d1ccba76.summary: From an empty Templates list, the user creates a draft template, fills content, and publishes it as a new version.
steps: Templates with nothing listed yet; Create template
Blank draft editor with Draft badge
Publish New Version: slide to publish
Library grid with new template card
steal: The empty list offers to create a new template or import one, with 'Create' in two places.
A Draft label stays beside the title until the template is published.
The 'Publish New Version' pop-up shows '✓ No warnings' and asks you to slide to publish.
A blank page offers 'Pick a template', 'Upload HTML' and typed / commands to add content.
avoid: The extra slide-to-publish step should be kept for going live, not for every routine save of a scenario.
mobbin:8914ef26-a0a5-4618-a806-8d1ccba76.fit: Scenario manager: add clear draft and published versions, with a check before publishing. It supports replacing Word and paper with a basic editor, not a Maestro rebuild.

mobbin:62ac5b2e-bca0-4c6c-95c5-3a11fa133.summary: In the draft editor, the user opens 'View History', picks a past version, and restores it while keeping the current version.
steal: Version history opens as a side panel over the editor, so you do not leave the page.
The confirmation explains that restoring creates a new version and keeps the current content in the history.
Each history entry shows how long ago it was saved and who saved it.
After restoring, the template stays in Draft, so it still has to be published to go live.
mobbin:62ac5b2e-bca0-4c6c-95c5-3a11fa133.fit: Scenario manager: fills a known gap, because the SCE editor cannot restore old versions clearly. Restoring without losing anything protects faculty work, unlike today's checklists, which lose data when the window closes.
